ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory dual-layer screening: (1) institution-level screening by the Swiss confirming, paying, and correspondent banks under GwG Arts. 3-6 and CDB 20 against FATF, UN Security Council, Switzerland SECO, OFAC, and EU consolidated sanctions lists, with PEP database cross-matching and enhanced due diligence on any positive hit or politically exposed person connection; (2) corporate-level screening of all UBOs, directors, beneficial shareholders, and material counterparties in the milk powder commodity chain using automated tools against the SECO Embargo Act list, UN Consolidated List, and reputable commercial PEP/sanctions registries, retaining documented screening evidence for a minimum of 5 years per GwG record-keeping rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Zentraler Firmenindex des Eidgenössischen Amts für das Handelsregister (https://www.zefix.ch)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory doctrine: the company name of an Aktiengesellschaft must be written in Latin script using a Swiss national language (German, French, Italian, Romansh) or a clear internationally accepted transliteration; purely foreign script names (Cyrillic, Arabic, CJK) are admitted only in Latin transliteration. The name must satisfy OR Art. 950 principles of firm-wahrheit (truthfulness), firm-klarheit (clarity), and firm-unterscheidbarkeit (distinctiveness), must not mislead about the legal form, territory, or business scope, and must include the mandatory legal form indicator 'Aktiengesellschaft' or 'AG', with 'SA' equally accepted in French-speaking cantons.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: National institution tokens: 'Swiss', 'Schweizerisch', 'Confédération suisse', 'Eidgenossenschaft', 'Bund', 'SBB' (require specific government authorization under the Federal Coat of Arms and Public Signs Protection Act, SR 232.21 and the Swissness legislation)
Banking and financial services tokens: 'Bank', 'Finanz', 'Versicherung', 'Fonds', 'Vorsorge' (require prior FINMA or insurance supervisory licensing)
Trust and fiduciary tokens: 'Trust', 'Treuhand', 'Fiduciaire' (require licensed trustee/fiduciary approval or professional qualification evidence)
Business-scope misrepresentation tokens: 'Export', 'Import', 'Commodity', 'Dairy', 'Milch' (prohibited where the stated or implied activity is not actually carried out)
Identical or confusingly similar tokens of pre-existing registered firms and protected federal/cantonal arms or public trademarks
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No statutory long-term reservation exists in Switzerland; the name pre-clearance enquiry by the cantonal commercial register office is valid for a maximum of 30 days and must be reused in the notarial deed before expiry. Upon formal rejection, the applicant must file a written administrative appeal with the cantonal supervisory authority over commercial registers (Aufsichtsbehörde über das Handelsregister) within 30 days of receipt of the negative order (Art. 940e OR and Art. 52 HRegV), setting out legal grounds and alternative name proposals; the supervisory authority will render a reasoned written decision. Further appeal lies to the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht) within 30 days. In parallel, the applicant may immediately re-submit a revised, compliant name proposal to the same cantonal commercial register office, which routinely accelerates clearance.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Full virtual or post-office-box addresses are rejected. The AG must possess a physically identifiable registered office in a Swiss municipality, generally where its actual business administration is located (Art. 51a and Art. 643 OR). For this commodity trading industry, licensed domiciliation and administrative services (Domizilgesellschaft/domiciliation fiduciaire under Art. 13a HRegV) are permissible provided the domicile service provider maintains a physical office, holds the required police or cantonal license, the true central administration remains attributable to the company, and a written domiciliation agreement is executed.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate for this standard-risk trading tier. Estimated probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the commercial register authority or local police within the first incorporation year is 12%; probability increases to approximately 25% where a third-party licensed domiciliation provider is used or where a PEP/sanctions alert arises during KYC screening.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR) Articles 61, 620-640 (Aktiengesellschaft formation), 626 (capital), 629 (registration), and 632 (paid-up minimum).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Kantonales Handelsregisteramt); federal oversight by the Federal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt des Bundes, HRAB).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Organisation articles and deed of incorporation (Statuten und Gründungsurkunde), notarized and filed via PRC / ZH.portal or equivalent cantonal eRegistry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital CHF 100,000, of which at least CHF 50,000 must be paid up. Funds must be deposited in a blocking (escrow) account at a Swiss bank and confirmed by a blocking confirmation (Sperrbestätigung) prior to registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED AND AGREED by the first board of directors that the share subscriptions shown in the subscription list are approved and the fully paid-up share capital of CHF 100,000 is acknowledged; that the registered office is adopted at the address in Zug, Switzerland; that the officers are appointed as follows: director A, director B, and secretary C; that the articles of association and formation documents are ratified; and that the board shall file the company for registration with the commercial register, obtain all required permits, and open a bank account. The statutory capital remains blocked until confirmation of registration. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation and pre-verification of company name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Zug) and federal name database (Zefix).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request with three proposed name variants. Ensure the name is not identical to or confusingly similar to an existing registered Swiss entity and does not contain prohibited terms. Provide a short description of the corporate purpose (raw milk powder commodity trading).
required_dossiers: Copy of passport or ID of all shareholders and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, revise and resubmit the request with a different name; obtain a formal refusal note and file an administrative objection to the commercial register office within 10 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial execution of articles of association and share subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss notary public (Notar) in the canton of Zug.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Sign and notarize the deed of incorporation, including the articles of association (Statuten), list of directors, registered office address, and share subscriptions. The notary authenticates the signatures and ensures the corporate purpose complies with Swiss law.
required_dossiers: Valid identification of all founders and subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises formal defects, correct the articles and re-sign before the same notary; if the applicant is rejected for insufficient documentation, provide supplementary declarations and obtain a new hearing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening blocking account and paying up share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank (e.g., cantonal bank or private bank) in Zug.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the name of the company 'CH AG in formation'. Deposit the required minimum paid-up capital (CHF 50,000 or more). Instruct the bank to issue a blocking confirmation (Sperrbestätigung) confirming the funds are frozen for the benefit of the commercial register.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of directors and share signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account application due to diligence gaps, provide additional proof of the commercial purpose and source of funds; request escalation to the bank's compliance officer or select an alternative licensed bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing for registration with the commercial register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized deed, blocking confirmation, and all signed forms to the commercial register office via the approved eRegistry portal or in person. The office verifies compliance with OR Article 629 and issues the certificate of registration (Handelsregisterauszug). Legal personality arises upon completion of registration.
required_dossiers: Certified copies of articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond in writing to the objections raised by the commercial registrar within 30 days; correct any inaccuracies in the forms, supplement missing evidence, or request an oral hearing for reconsideration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (FTA), Cantonal Tax Office of Zug, Suva (workers compensation), and local municipality.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration, apply for a VAT number (MWST), company tax identification number, and employer social insurance registration. Register as a food business operator with the competent food safety authority if trading in milk powder. Complete any municipal business license filings.
required_dossiers: Commercial register excerpt and registration number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT or tax identification application is delayed, contact the FTA tax number service directly and provide the registration excerpt; for food business approval objections, submit updated HACCP documentation to the relevant cantonal authority within 20 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (Bundesamt für Lebensmittelsicherheit und Veterinärwesen, BLV, now integrated in the Federal Health Office (BAG) as food-safety division) together with the Cantonal Food Control Authority (Kantonale Lebensmittelkontrolle).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business Operator Approval for Trade Supply and Import of Milk Powder (Lebensmittelbetriebs-Bewilligung für den Handel mit Milchpulver).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (Bundesamt für Umwelt, BAFU) and Cantonal Environmental Protection Office (Amt für Umweltschutz Zug).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / Exempt – no full EIA report required for pure commodity trading operations without manufacturing, packing, or dairy processing; only a simplified environmental registration with the cantonal office is necessary if goods are handled in leased warehouses.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A for trading-only activity. If warehouses or repacking are present, comply with the Swiss Water Protection Ordinance (Gewässerschutzverordnung, GSchV) for any washing water, the Clean Air Act (Luftreinhalte-Verordnung, LRV) for volatile organic compounds, and the Waste and Packaging Regulation (VVV) for waste handling.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Cantonal Fire Prevention Service (Feuerpolizei) for the registered office and warehouses; structural load inspection or floor-load certificate if storage is used; occupational safety clearance per SUVA (Swiss Accident Insurance Fund) and the Labour Law (Arbeitsgesetz) for premises, including an internal accident prevention plan and first aid availability.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC); cantonal tax authorities; portal: www.estv.admin.ch / ePortal VAT services
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft must first notarize the articles of association and register with the cantonal commercial registry, thereby obtaining the permanent Swiss company UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer / Numéro d'identification des entreprises). The UID is issued by the Federal Statistical Office through the cantonal register. VAT registration with the ESTV must be made separately via the ePortal/e-REG form once taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 or voluntarily if thresholds are not met. The UID is used as the VAT identification number and must be listed on invoices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland has no general check-the-box classification. An AG is per se a taxable legal entity subject to federal, cantonal, and communal income tax. Certain hybrid mismatch elections are available under Swiss implementation of BEPS Action 2 for foreign hybrid instruments or entities, and qualified Swiss holding or finance companies may opt for deemed substance tax transparency in specific intra-group financing structures. No US-style pass-through election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (VAT / Mehrwertsteuer / TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual worldwide turnover from taxable supplies (excluding real estate costs; Art. 10 para. 2 lit. a MWSTG); voluntary registration permitted for businesses below threshold; special lower thresholds apply for certain marginal activities
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing is permitted but not mandatory. There is no domestic real-time fiscal clearance API or digital stamping mandate. All invoices must contain the UID and VAT rate; QR-billing standards apply for payment references. Export VAT substantiation requires electronic customs declarations using Swiss Customs e-dec/NCTS; attested export documents must be retained for audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to supplies of goods transported from Switzerland to foreign jurisdictions where legal ownership passes to the recipient abroad, including cross-border commodity trading in raw milk powder, provided the supplier retains export proof. Services relating to movable goods destined for foreign use may also be zero-rated. The supply must be demonstrably delivered outside Switzerland with the Swiss customs export declaration confirming exit.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Swiss e-dec / NCTS declaration with accepted export summary)
Transport Document (Bill of Lading for sea freight, CMR for road, or Air Waybill for air freight)
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 wire evidence showing repatriation of proceeds from foreign buyer
Sales contract or order confirmation stating Incoterms and delivery destination
Export delivery certificate (Lieferschein) and, where applicable, customs transit accompanying document T1/T2
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under Swiss VAT law, export zero-rating is strictly audited against the full evidential chain. Missing, false, or contradictory export documentation triggers retroactive VAT assessment at the applicable rate (8.1% standard or 2.6% reduced for foodstuffs) with statutory interest. Fraudulent or deliberate misdeclaration may lead to penalties up to 30% of the assessed tax, plus further tax evasion fines and criminal penalties under Art. 186-187 MWSTG. The statute of limitation for clawback is generally 10 years from the end of the year in which the supply was made.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) / Schweizerische Nationalbank, Bundesplatz 1, CH-3003 Bern, operating under the Currency and Payment Act of 22 December 1999 and the Federal Act on the Free Movement of Capital (Capital Transactions Act, revised 1995). SNB overseers the Swiss Interbank Clearing (SIC) system and publishes FX statistics.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full and unrestricted convertibility of the Swiss franc (CHF) on both current and capital accounts. No exchange controls, no licensing of currency transactions, and no central bank approval is required for foreign investment, profit repatriation, dividend distribution, or royalty payments. Profits may be remitted freely, subject only to federal withholding tax on dividends (35% statutory rate, typically reduced to 0% for qualifying domestic/inbound holdings or to treaty-lowered rates for treaty residents through an actuality match) and standard corporate taxation. The Capital Transactions Act explicitly guarantees the free movement of capital, rendering any repatriation-limiting restrictions inapplicable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender requirement, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation timeline for export proceeds in Switzerland. Exporters are free to hold foreign currency in Swiss or foreign bank accounts indefinitely. The SNB collects statistical data on cross-border payments for balance-of-payments purposes but imposes no currency conversion mandate. For dairy commodity traders, export invoices in EUR, USD, or other freely convertible currencies can be retained offshore or converted into CHF at market rates at the discretion of the treasury.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Trade Finance Account (with Capital Escrow sub-account capability)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Pictet & Cie (Luxembourg/Frankfurt for corporate lending, Geneva private bank for treasury)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.onboarding_viability_tier: Low (selective for pure commodity trading without asset-based relationship)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with significant legal constraints. Switzerland is not an EEA member, and EU/UK electronic money institution (EMI) passports do not extend into Switzerland. An offshore EMI (e.g., Revolut Business EU, Wise Business, or a Lithuania-regulated EMI) cannot accept Swiss-resident deposits or provide Swiss IBAN accounts with full SIC/CHF clearing access without obtaining a FINMA banking license or entering into a white-label arrangement with a licensed Swiss bank. Alternatively, fintech banks with FINMA licenses (e.g., Sygnum Bank, SEBA Bank, Yuh, radicant) can serve the entity, but they typically focus on digital assets or basic cash services and may lack trade finance infrastructure (LC issuance, commodity trade settlement). Therefore, the recommended structure is a fintech account as a secondary liquidity tranche, not as the primary treasury rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FINMA Circular 20/2 and the AMLO ordinance permit remote/video identification under an equivalence-of-security protocol, but in practice the vast majority of Swiss universal banks (UBS, ZKB, BCV) mandate an in-person KYC interview with the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) and the signatory directors of the CH_AG for commodity trading entities, particularly where the shareholder is non-resident. Remote opening is generally possible at FINMA-licensed fintech banks and certain cantonal banks if the beneficial ownership structure is simple, the domicile is in a low-risk jurisdiction (Switzerland), and the business is rated Low-Risk Standard (ISIC 4633). A physical presence in the form of registered Swiss office with actual economic substance (employees, premises, board meetings) remains the strongest de-risking factor and materially accelerates onboarding timelines from 6-10 weeks to 2-4 weeks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Onboarding red flag: Juridical personality is a freshly incorporated AG (registration less than 12 months) with a single non-resident shareholder and no independent Swiss management substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified commercial registry extract (Handelsregisterauszug) evidencing original incorporation; signed Board resolution mandating an independent Swiss-resident director or compliance officer; executed shareholding declaration with source-of-funds breakdown; corporate group structure chart; initial capital contribution wire covering memo referencing the bank account agreement; physical leased office contract and payroll records of Swiss employees; Swiss VAT registration certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure: Existing or pending trade counterparties domiciled in high-risk or partially sanctioned jurisdictions (e.g., Russia, Belarus, Iran, Syria) within the dairy supply chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country-specific trade embargo compliance policy signed by the Board; complete and verifiable list of all counterparty passport/vat numbers; end-beneficiary declarations for each offloading facility; certificate of origin (EUR.1 / Form A) and consular invoices; inspection certificates from SGS, Bureau Veritas, or Intertek confirming the physical goods do not originate from sanctioned territories; internal sanctions screening tool report for each counterparty; export/import end-user certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Product discrepancy: The bank template for 'raw milk powder' trade flags a possible PMO (Product Marketing Order) exemption mismatch or appearance of a quasi-agricultural cooperative profile not aligned with a conservative commodities bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ISIC/NAICS classification certificate issued by the Swiss Customs Administration (EZV) confirming the ISIC 4633 classification; food-grade import/export permits from Swiss Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (BLV/FSVO) and the EU Health Certificate for dairy products; warehouse warrant of a licensed Swiss storage company (e.g., Peregrine, Volcafe or an SGS-supervised silo) holding milk powder lots; documentary trade flow chart showing the purchase from dairy cooperative and resale to off-takers; shipment copies of the international B/L and container temperature logs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner opacity: Multi-tier offshore holding structure above the direct shareholder of the CH_AG.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full chain ownership diagram through every entity up to the ultimate natural persons; official registry extracts (Companies House, Delaware, Hong Kong CR, etc.) of all intermediate holding vehicles; shareholder register stamped by the transfer agent; proof of identity (passport notarized) and proof of address of each UBO; completion of the bank's standard UBO declaration form with source-of-wealth and source-of-funds questionnaire; independent third-party due-diligence report (e.g., Thomson Reuters, Dow Jones Risk) demonstrating the absence of negative media or politically exposed persons (PEPs).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The CHF capital injection of CHF 100,000 (minimum capital) is routed via the SIC payment system (if the sending bank has a Swiss branch) or via SWIFT MT103 with the beneficiary bank's SWIFT/BIC code and the CH_AG's CHF IBAN (CHxx 0079 0042 ... ). Recommended purpose code in SWIFT field 70/33B: 'CAPIN' (Capital Injection) or 'COST' if it represents a shareholder contribution; reference must include 'Capital increase / Einzahlung Aktienkapital' and the Commercial Register registration number. When routed via SEPA (EUR) as an alternative, the ISO 20022 purpose code must be 'CAPC'. A supporting shareholder resolution and a confirmation from the bank's registrar evidencing the credit of the capital contribution to account passbook (Aktieneinzahlung) is required by the bank to issue the confirmation of paid-up capital.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails for dairy commodity settlement: (1) SWIFT MT103 / MT103 STP for direct telegraphic transfers to global off-takers and dairy cooperatives, with the commercial invoice, B/L, and Certificate of Origin referenced in field 70; (2) Documentary letters of credit (commercial LC) issued in compliance with UCP 600 (MT700/MT707), with the milk powder shipment documents (inspection certificate, health certificate, B/L, commercial invoice, and insurance policy) being negotiated against the LC terms; (3) Domestic Swiss payments processed via SIC (CHF) with instant or next-day clearing; (4) EUR-denominated intra-European settlements using SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) with mandatory intention of field 'Remittance information'; (5) For USD-denominated liquid trades, adopting the Fedwire/CHIPS corridor via the bank's New York correspondent. The instructed XCCY rails should presuppose an LC confirmation from a highly rated third-party bank (minimum A-) for large transactions to eliminate settlement risk.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (Outright) in CHF/USD, CHF/EUR—settled through CLS or SIC, with standard short-dated to 12-month tenors, no underlying transaction documentation required under Swiss law.
FX Swaps (Spot-Forward Combination) for treasury cash-flow management in USD/CHF and EUR/CHF.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) limited to non-convertible emerging-market currencies (e.g., CNY, INR) of dairy importing countries, with fixing reference to a market-verified rate (Reuters/Bloomberg), stored as permissible OTC under Swiss FMIA derivative clearing thresholds.
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (XCCY) for medium-term matching of CHF liability against USD/CHF P&L, permitted under FINMA margin rules for non-financial end-users.
Vanilla FX Options (European style) for insurance-like hedging of adverse USD/CHF moves, with premium settled in CHF.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) approval of annual financial statements and discharge of the Board (Art. 698(2) OR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' Meeting (internal corporate body); AGM minutes kept on-site; no automatic Handelsregister filing unless registered details change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after FYE; a 31-December FYE requires the AGM by 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Judicial dissolution order under Art. 731b OR after register-office warning; director liability for unlawful AGM default; no monetary penalty from the state

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (federal, cantonal and communal profit tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (Zug/Kantonale Steuerverwaltung) for the combined federal (ESTV) and cantonal/communal assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Cantonal summons (Merkblatt) requires filing typically within 1-6 months of issuance; statutory maximum 6 months after FYE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Arrears interest of 0.5%-4.5%, procedural fines for filing obstruction, penal fines up to 30% of evaded tax for negligence (Art. 175 DBG) and up to 250% plus confinement for intentional evasion (Art. 176 DBG); discretionary tax assessment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return (Mehrwertsteuer-Abrechnung) submitted via the ESTV e-service 'Swiss Federal Tax Portal'
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 60 days after the close of the VAT reporting period; calendar-year period: by 1 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Reminder charges (CHF 30-100), default interest of about 5%, administrative fine up to CHF 30,000 or 30% of tax evaded (Art. 70-72 MWSTG), criminal penalties for deliberate fiscal fraud (Art. 73 MWSTG)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer annual wage declaration and final AHV social-security accounting (Lohnausweis / ELM)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: AHV Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse) of the employer's trade or canton
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Final prior-year salary declaration by 31 January of the following year per compensation-office practice; quarterly interim settlements continue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Arrears interest of 5% on unpaid contributions; administrative penalties and penal fines under Art. 86-87 AHVG; forced debt collection and director liability for unpaid employer contributions

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary statutory audit is mandatory if the company exceeds two of the three thresholds for two consecutive years: balance-sheet total above CHF 20 million; turnover above CHF 40 million; average annual headcount above 250 (Art. 727 OR). A limited audit is required for all other companies unless the shareholders unanimously opt out under the small-company exemption (fewer than 10 FTEs, total assets below CHF 2 million, turnover below CHF 2 million).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957-963b) and Swiss GAAP FER for the statutory annual financial statements; IFRS or US GAAP may be adopted voluntarily; additional FINMA reporting applies only to licensed financial intermediaries.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Art. 697j-697m OR the Board maintains a private register of beneficial owners holding 25% or more of shares or voting rights; owners must disclose upon request and any transfer mandates an immediate register update. There is no annual public refiling in Switzerland, but the register must be available on-site for review by tax, AML, corporate-register and judicial authorities; intentional false or missing disclosure is punishable by fines up to CHF 500,000.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Board of Directors and Signatory Register (Handelsregister record)
Minutes of Shareholders' and Board Meetings
Commercial books, vouchers and annual financial statements

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 3,000 - 9,000 per year (CHF 2,500 - 7,500) for registered office, corporate secretarial and registered-agent services in Zug/Zurich
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - 25,000 for a limited statutory audit; USD 30,000 - 75,000 for a full ordinary audit of a dairy commodity trading AG, depending on turnover magnitude and group structure

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal statutory corporate income tax: 8.5% on post-tax profit (effective 7.83% on pre-tax profit); cantonal/communal rates add approximately 11.9%-21.0% combined effective burden. In Canton Zug, the strategic seat of the entity, the effective combined rate is approximately 11.9%-14.6%, one of the lowest in Switzerland.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Swiss Tax Reform and AHV Financing Act (STAF/OTR 2020) introduces patent box relief (up to 90% income exemption), cantonal R&D super-deduction (up to 150%), participation relief for qualifying dividend income, and tax-free repayment of capital contribution reserves. Cantonal structural/innovation incentives may grant temporary tax relief up to 10 years for newly relocated or newly established companies. No open-ended tax holidays exist.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined cantonal/communal and federal corporate income tax return for legal persons (e.g., Canton Zug 'Steuererklärung juristische Personen' / Form St 1). E-filing is conducted through the official cantonal tax administration portal or certified Swiss tax software, with the Swiss Unified Business Identifier (UID) as mandatory taxpayer reference; the same return serves for Federal Direct Tax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Tax period equals the financial year. The return must be filed within six months after financial year-end; for a calendar-year AG, the standard deadline is 30 June of the following year. Extensions may be granted only on timely written application, generally up to 31 December. Quarterly provisional instalments are payable in advance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered seat, share capital, UID (CHE number), ISIC 4633 principal business activity (milk powder wholesale and commodity trading), financial year, employees, balance sheet total.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Swiss AG must be portrayed as a managed Swiss entity: Swiss office address, Swiss management, Swiss bank mandates and independent commercial correspondence. A foreign-directed company with no Swiss operation will fail substance assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Share capital per Swiss Code of Obligations (minimum CHF 100,000; 20% paid in, at least CHF 50,000) plus statutory reserves and capital contribution reserves from non-resident shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Paid-in capital from non-resident shareholders must be booked separately as 'reserves from capital contributions' to preserve tax-free repayment ability and avoid 35% Swiss dividend withholding tax on return of capital.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / Gross Profit from Dairy Commodity Trading
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Worldwide turnover from commodity trading in whole and skimmed milk powder, cost of sales, gross margin, net profit before tax, intercompany contracts and transfer pricing documentation for purchases/sales within the group.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Profit is attributed to Switzerland based on the Swiss AG's functions, assets, personnel and risks. Pure title-passing or booking-centre activity with no Swiss decision-making will be reattributed to the foreign principal.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Relief for qualifying dividend income and capital gains from participations of at least 10% of share capital or CHF 1 million market value with minimum holding of one year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This deduction does not apply to active milk powder trading income. Non-resident shareholders cannot claim the relief on Swiss AG operating profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit for Federal Direct Tax and Cantonal Tax after application of participation relief, patent box, loss carry-forward (7-year limitation), and any deemed-interest or equity interest adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Swiss AG is assessed at entity level. Foreign owners have no direct income tax liability on Swiss AG profits until distribution. Cross-border TP adjustments must be mirrored in the foreign parent's books to avoid double non-taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of gross dividends paid or credited to shareholders, computation of 35% Verrechnungssteuer, and remittance to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA) with the corresponding VSt account statement (SwissTax portal / FTA WHT clearing).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders may benefit from treaty-reduced rates only after the Swiss payer correctly withholds 35% and the foreign recipient applies for refund, or where FTA has pre-approved reduced withholding at source through an approval procedure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a reminder and procedural fines commonly ranging from CHF 100 to CHF 10,000. Default interest accrues at 4.75% p.a. (2024 FTA reference). Deliberate or repeated non-filing allows the tax authority to estimate profits with a security surcharge on Swiss-source revenue and may escalate to criminal tax proceedings with fines up to three times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss Verrechnungssteuer on gross dividends paid or credited by the Swiss AG. Reduced DTA rates (commonly 0%-15%, with 5%-15% for qualified shareholdings, subject to each treaty) apply only through FTA refund or prior FTA approval for reduced withholding at source.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder applies to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration using the official 'Antrag auf Rückerstattung der Verrechnungssteuer' (Swiss withholding tax refund form), attaching an original Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, evidence of dividend payment, and proof of 35% withholding. Refund applications must be submitted within three years from the end of the calendar year in which the dividend became due. For ongoing relief, the Swiss payer may apply to the FTA for prior approval of reduced treaty withholding at source; approval requires confirmation of the beneficial owner, holding period and full tax liability in the residence state. No refund will be granted to a shareholder who is not beneficial owner or who fails the anti-abuse/PPT test.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% statutory Swiss withholding tax; no WHT is levied on license or franchise fees under Swiss domestic law, and Swiss DTA rates are therefore usually 0% (sometimes 5%-10% where a different source concept applies). Interest: ordinary intercompany loan interest and seller's note interest are subject to 0% Swiss WHT; interest on bonds, money market paper and bank deposits is subject to the 35% Verrechnungssteuer. Treaty rates for bond interest typically range from 0% to 10%; refund or prior approval procedure is required for treaty protection.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Country-by-Country Reporting mandatory for MNE groups with consolidated group revenue of at least CHF 900 million. Full OECD Master File and Local File documentation is expected by the FTA when annual cross-border related-party transactions exceed CHF 5 million; reduced documentation may suffice below this threshold. All TP files must be submitted on formal request within 30-60 days.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not operate an industry-based Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) statute comparable to UAE or Caribbean regimes. However, substantive economic substance is a hard requirement derived from Art. 58 and Art. 65 DBG, the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines, the Multilateral Instrument principal purpose test and Swiss anti-abuse case law: the Swiss AG must demonstrate actual local management, physical premises, qualified staff, independent decision-making, real intercompany contracts, and genuine commercial risk absorption. A letterbox company that merely routes milk powder trade flows or holds invoices without operational functions will be denied treaty benefits, participation relief and possibly reclassified as a sham.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful submission of false or incomplete tax returns; off-book sales revenues from whole or skimmed milk powder transactions; inflated cost of goods sold; fictitious intercompany commissions; fabricated invoices from shell trading companies; concealment of bank receivables in Switzerland.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax evasion penalty of up to three times the amount of tax evaded (DBG Art. 175), plus default interest of 4.75% p.a. Tax fraud through forged records (DBG Art. 186) entails criminal fines and imprisonment of responsible officers for up to five years, confiscation of illicit profits and publication of the conviction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable under Art. 754 OR for corporate losses caused by wilful or negligent mismanagement, including unpaid corporate taxes. Where the company is insolvent, tax authorities recover the unpaid tax directly from the responsible directors. Criminal imprisonment of up to 5 years, travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed during proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distribution or deemed distribution of profits to non-resident shareholders without deduction and remittance of the 35% Swiss dividend withholding tax; unlawful reliance on treaty exemptions without FTA approval; disposal of capital contribution reserves without segregating taxable dividend amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The FTA recovers the full 35% WHT from the Swiss AG plus interest at 4.75%, irrespective of the beneficiary's treaty position. Criminal prosecutions may impose fines of up to CHF 30,000 on the company and its responsible executives. The company is barred from effective treaty relief for all shareholders during the default period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly distribute dividends without WHT in liquidation or asset-deficiency scenarios are personally liable for the withheld amounts under Swiss withholding tax responsibility rules. Directors face criminal charges for participation in the infringement and personal travel bans pending final payment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Structure and Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Swiss AG with no employees, no leased Swiss premises, all bank mandates and trading decisions executed from abroad; booking of milk powder commodity trades through Swiss entity solely to access DTA advantages, obtain a Swiss bank account, or create artificial margin allocation (TNMM below 0%-1%); nominee directors without operational control.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization and upward adjustment of Swiss taxable profit by the FTA; denial of treaty benefits under the principal purpose test; cancellation of participation relief and refund of dividend WHT; back taxes plus interest; potential requalification of the Swiss AG as a transparent conduit resulting in immediate taxation at the level of the beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who allow the company to operate as a letterbox may face civil restitution for the benefit obtained by the foreign shareholders, personal liability for uncollectable taxes, criminal prosecution for aiding tax evasion of hidden principals, imprisonment up to three years for accessory acts, and confiscation of their personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealment of the true ultimate beneficial owner through bearer share arrangements or nominee directors; accepting commodity settlement payments through unexplained third-party accounts contrary to the declared SWIFT LC / TT wire payment rails; dealing with sanctioned counterparties or politically exposed persons without AML due diligence; deliberate falsification of commodity trade documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines under Anti-Money Laundering Act Art. 21-23 of up to CHF 500,000 per violation; disciplinary measures by self-regulatory organizations; confiscation of proceeds under Art. 70 Swiss Criminal Code; exclusion from Swiss banking relationships and cancellation of the tax clearance certificate for commercial registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally exposed to imprisonment of up to three years for money laundering (Art. 305bis SCC) or five years for participation in a criminal organization (Art. 260ter SCC); personal travel bans, asset freezes, and joint and several civil liability for repatriation of diverted funds. Directors cannot rely on corporate indemnity where their personal criminal conduct is proven.
